title: Harrowgate Under Water
briefing: Overnight rain flooded Harrowgate's loading bays. Stock on the floor is ruined; racking and the main store are dry. The insurer's loss adjuster arrives tomorrow.
Hollis Varga asks you to manage the claim and the lessons.

evidence.title: Damage summary
evidence.body: Floor-level stock lost: about 120,000. Two forklifts water-damaged (about 30,000). Loading bays closed for 3 days.

evidence.title: Insurance
evidence.body: Flood excess 250,000 per event; cover limit 1,000,000.

evidence.title: Earlier decision
evidence.body: Your flood appraisal recommended a response plan; it was not adopted.

questions.prompt: How much will the insurer pay for this event?

options.label: Nothing: the loss (about 150,000 including forklifts) is below the 250,000 excess
options.feedback: Below the excess, Valtren keeps it all, which is what the 'net' analysis showed.

options.label: 150,000 minus a small deductible
options.feedback: The excess is 250,000, larger than the loss.

options.label: Adopt the response plan now (raised racking, sandbag store, stock-move procedure) and ask Brantwell to quote a lower excess
options.feedback: The cheap mitigation is still the right one.

options.label: Build the barriers now
options.feedback: The appraisal hasn't changed; one flood doesn't change the probability.

options.label: Nothing: floods are rare
options.feedback: One just happened, and Valtren paid all of it.

questions.prompt: How do you deal with the loss adjuster?

options.label: Provide photos, stock and asset records and repair quotes, and confirm in writing that the loss is below the excess
options.feedback: Accurate records, even when no payment is due, support future claims.

options.label: Add new forklifts to the claim to get above the excess
options.feedback: Inflating a claim is insurance fraud.

questions.prompt: How do you report the event to Hollis?

options.label: Loss, what insurance covers (nothing), why, and the plan; including that the earlier recommendation wasn't adopted
Remind him you warned about this
Describe it as minor
options.feedback: 150,000 kept by Valtren is not minor.

lesson: Insurance protects against the big loss, not the frequent one. Small floods are yours to pay, so cheap mitigation pays. Report candidly, without scoring points.
